verifyNote: Written from the long standing published ACX requirements. The official page needs a web browser and could not be read while this file was made, so compare every number with the source before you record or hire a narrator.

credits.closing: This has been {title}. Written by {author}. Narrated by {narrator}. Copyright {year} by {holder}. Production copyright {productionYear} by {publisher}.

requirements.title: One chapter or section in each file
requirements.text: Each file holds one chapter or section and starts with its heading read aloud (for example "Chapter One").

requirements.title: Opening and closing credits
requirements.text: The audiobook has opening credits and closing credits, each as a file of its own.

requirements.title: Retail sample
requirements.text: A sample of one to five minutes, without credits or music at its start, as a file of its own.

requirements.title: Room tone at both ends
requirements.text: Each file has 0.5 to 1 second of room tone at the beginning and 1 to 5 seconds at the end.

requirements.title: Loudness
requirements.text: Each file measures between -23 dB and -18 dB RMS.

requirements.title: Peaks
requirements.text: Peak values are no higher than -3 dB.

requirements.title: Noise floor
requirements.text: The noise floor is no higher than -60 dB RMS.

requirements.title: File format
requirements.text: MP3, 192 kbps or higher, constant bit rate (CBR), at 44.1 kHz.

requirements.title: Mono or stereo
requirements.text: All files are in the same channel format: all mono or all stereo.

requirements.title: Length of a file
requirements.text: No file is longer than 120 minutes. A longer chapter is split into parts.

requirements.title: Consistent sound
requirements.text: Sound, spacing and pronunciation are consistent across all files, and the narration matches the text of the book.

requirements.title: Narration
requirements.text: Check the platform's current rule on narration by a person or by a synthetic voice before you choose.

notes: The app prepares the script, the list of files and the pronunciation guide. It does not measure sound: loudness, peaks and noise floor are checked in your recording program or with the platform's own checker.
wordsPerFinishedHour is the figure commonly used to estimate finished audio length from a word count. Narrators differ; ask yours.
Other audiobook distributors publish their own requirements. If you use one, replace the list above with theirs and name the source.
